tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description begins with 'Use this skill when the user wants to understand or cut Amazon Bedrock spend, or check Bedrock capacity, even if they don't call it a cost review', which is imperative phrasing focused on user intent (cost/capacity goals rather than internal mechanics). It extensively lists explicit trigger contexts (high/low bills, token mismatches, pricing tiers, PT idle/EOL, quotas, throttling, latency, log retention, pasted CloudWatch/Cost Explorer output) covering a wide range of indirect phrasings a user might use, and explicitly excludes an out-of-scope case ('Not for outages happening now'). While long, it is a single sentence-paragraph consistent with being pushy/thorough about trigger coverage, which is explicitly called for in the test criteria.
tests.evidence: Use this skill when the user wants to understand or cut Amazon Bedrock spend, or check Bedrock capacity, even if they don't call it a cost review, for example why the bill is high or suspiciously low... Not for outages happening now.

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body avoids explaining general concepts (what is Bedrock, what is CloudWatch, etc.) and jumps straight into domain-specific conventions: exact API fields, usage-type suffixes, token types, quota naming. It is dense but every sentence conveys non-obvious domain knowledge the agent wouldn't otherwise have.
tests.evidence: "Usage types vary (`-mantle-`, `-standard`, `-flex`, `-priority`, `-cross-region-global`): match a model's lines loosely."

tests.name: Detailed reference materials must not be in body
tests.reasoning: The body keeps detailed reference tables (API quirks, metric definitions, quota codes, alarm thresholds) in separate reference files and only embeds a compact router table and short per-step pointers in the body itself, linking out for the heavy material.
tests.evidence: "How to read each API and metric: [collection-reference.md](references/collection-reference.md) (load it with any row)."

tests.name: Reference files must be linked
tests.reasoning: Every file under references/ is linked with a markdown link somewhere in the body (cost-analysis.md, checks-model-invocation.md, cloudwatch-alarm-reference.md, collection-reference.md, api-quirks.md, metrics-and-logs.md, quota-codes.md, related-skills.md).
tests.evidence: "[cost-analysis.md](references/cost-analysis.md) (Steps 3–5, before any LLM-COST or LLM-PT finding); [checks-model-invocation.md](references/checks-model-invocation.md) ..."

tests.name: Reference links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: Each reference link is paired with a specific trigger condition describing when to load it, both in the router table and in the final References section.

tests.name: Reference path format
tests.reasoning: All reference links use relative paths rooted at references/ with no absolute paths or traversal.
tests.evidence: "[api-quirks.md](references/api-quirks.md) (before interpreting a response; quota lookup §18, Step 6);"

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: Fragile operations (cost labeling, quota lookups, PT resize prohibition) are given exact prescriptive rules, while flexible/judgment-based areas (deciding Batch vs on-demand, model downsizing) are described with reasoning and criteria rather than rigid steps, matching prescriptiveness to fragility.
tests.evidence: "PT can't be resized in place (`UpdateProvisionedModelThroughput` changes only the name or model): give the LLM-PT-001 remediation, never an update command."

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: Where multiple sources could be used (e.g., pricing data), the skill establishes a clear priority order rather than presenting equal options.
tests.evidence: "Rates, in order: the user (say so); `pricing:GetProducts` (us-east-1, one call per model...); or the [pricing page](https://aws.amazon.com/bedrock/pricing/) read with `verify_aws_claim`."

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The procedure teaches a generalizable approach (scope, tokens, cost model, coverage check, checks, PT, headroom, alarms) applicable to any Bedrock cost/capacity review, not a one-off instance-specific task.
tests.evidence: "Run the steps in order. Each step is bounded: a denied API, no datapoints or an unsupported region is recorded as `unavailable` / `not checked` and the review goes on."

tests.name: Gotchas section
tests.reasoning: The skill includes a dedicated 'Common wrong answers' section plus an 'Error Handling' section documenting non-obvious environment-specific pitfalls and corrections an agent would otherwise get wrong.
tests.evidence: "'A `us.` profile bills as us-east-1.' It is a geographic routing scope; billing follows the source region (api-quirks §14, LLM-COST-005)."

tests.name: Templates and outputs missing
tests.reasoning: The skill produces structured cost/capacity review output and explicitly provides a report template asset for full reports.

tests.name: Templates and outputs must not be in body
tests.reasoning: No large inline output template exists in the body; the only table-like structure (quota report row) is short, and the full report template is kept in assets/.
tests.evidence: "Report the rows read as a table: | Quota name | Code | Applied value | Adjustable |, one row per quota"

tests.name: Asset files must be linked
tests.reasoning: The single asset file capacity-cost-report-template.md is referenced in the body via a markdown link.

tests.name: Asset links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: The asset link specifies the condition for loading it — only for a full report.

tests.name: Asset path format
tests.reasoning: The asset link uses a relative path rooted at assets/ with no absolute path or traversal.

tests.name: Step-by-step guidance
tests.reasoning: The procedural workflow is presented as an ordered checkbox checklist with 'Step N:' labels, matching the required format.
tests.evidence: "- [ ] Step 1: **Scope:** region(s), window, models and profiles...\n- [ ] Step 2: **Tokens:**..."

tests.name: Validation loops
tests.reasoning: The skill includes an explicit self-validation section instructing the agent to check its own output for errors before presenting, covering labeling, coverage checks, and divergence consistency.
tests.evidence: "## Before You Present — Validate Your Own Output\n\nA confidently wrong cost number is worse than a slow one. If an item can't be met, say so."
